questions.q: Why does the lesson recommend having three different versions of a capstone presentation ready?
options: Because a recruiter, a hiring manager, and a technical panel want different levels of detail, and using the wrong depth wastes time or reads as unprepared
Because the facts of the project change depending on the audience
Because only technical panels are ever allowed to ask questions
Because recruiters require a signed non-disclosure agreement to hear any version
questions.explain: The lesson explains that each audience wants a different depth of detail, so having tiered versions ready avoids wasting time or appearing unprepared.

questions.q: What is the first step in the lesson's five-step structure for presenting a capstone?
options: Showing the final dashboard
Reciting every object's API name
Describing the business problem the project actually addresses
Explaining what you'd do differently at scale
questions.explain: The lesson's structure starts with the business problem before moving into solution design, decisions, results, and scale considerations.

questions.q: What fictional company does the lesson use as the concrete example for the LTV Customer Management System capstone?
options: Northbridge Insurance Group
Fairmont Logistics
Cascadia Outdoor Supply
Cascade Foodservice Equipment Co.
questions.explain: The lesson references Cascade Foodservice Equipment Co., the fictional company used in the LTV Customer Management System capstone course.

questions.q: What backup plan does the lesson recommend in case a live org demo breaks?
options: Immediately ending the interview
Keeping screenshots or a short recording of the key screens ready
Reading the Apex code aloud instead
Switching to a completely different, unrelated project
questions.explain: The lesson recommends having screenshots or a recording ready so a technical failure doesn't derail the conversation.

questions.q: How does the lesson connect this lesson's presentation structure back to Lesson 4 (Portfolio Development)?
options: It says they are unrelated and should use different framing
It says only the written portfolio matters, and live presentation never does
It says Lesson 4's portfolio work should be deleted once you're in interviews
It frames the live presentation as the spoken version of the same README/case-study write-up, with consistent framing across all materials
questions.explain: The lesson explicitly ties the spoken presentation structure back to the written portfolio case study, recommending consistent framing across both.
